Here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable behavior and avoids matching the patched behavior:

```yaml
id: "vuln-countly-server-2bfa1ee1"
title: "Potential Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password Vulnerability"
description: "This rule checks if a password recovery mechanism is using a weak hash function (like SHA512) to generate the password reset ID."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - javascript
metadata:
  tags: ["security", "authentication"]
pattern: >-
  :warning
  $ = Import("./../../../api/utils/authorizer.js") && Import("./../../../api/utils/common.js") && Import("./../../../plugins/pluginManager.js") && Import("./../../../api/utils/rights.js") && Import("./../../../api/parts/mgmt/mail.js") && Import("./../../../api/parts/data/stats.js") && Import("request") && Import("url") && Import("crypto")
  $ = FunctionDeclaration > (
    body: (
      (
        (FunctionCall > MemberExpr[name="require"] arguments=["'argon2'"]) |
        (FunctionCall > MemberExpr[name="require"] arguments=["'./../../../api/utils/rights.js'"]).
      )
    )
  )
```

This rule will match if the `require` function is used to import any of the specified modules, which are known to be involved in the vulnerable behavior. The pattern checks for the presence of these imports without considering their exact location or order within the codebase.

Please note that this rule might not catch all possible instances of the vulnerability because it's based on static analysis and may not cover all possible ways the vulnerability could be exploited. It is recommended to perform a security code review for any changes in your codebase.
